# Alert

A message that stays on the page with the content it is about.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Brand expressive</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-alert--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:brand-expressive;mode:light" title="Alert examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-alert--docs">Open Alert in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-alert--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:brand-expressive;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Brand expressive:** A sign-up that did not go through, and how to recover, on the page. Not for confirmations; toast does that.

- **Use it when:** People need to read a standing notice or how to recover, on this page, tied to what they are doing.
- **Not when:** A short confirmation that can go away by itself, or one notice for the whole site.

Instead:

- [Toast](./toast.md): Short, non-blocking, goes away.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): Needs an answer before going on.
- Site banner: One full-width notice for the whole site.

## Why it works this way

Alert looks the way it does because of 4 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Alert, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-tasks-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How often do people repeat actions?</b><code>tasks.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Rarely</div><p>One action: sign up.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Alert</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>default</b>: Alerts here only report a sign-up that did not go through; confirmations go in a toast.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Input group: block-start</code> <code>Input group: block-end</code> <code>Toggle: lg</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Alert decision would reopen</small><p>and 2 answers that follow from it: <b>Three</b>, <b>Only what today's screens use</b>.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many tones does it use?</b><code>voice.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One per moment</div><p>Playful in headlines, plain in errors.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Alert</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>default</b>: Alerts here only report a sign-up that did not go through; confirmations go in a toast.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>destructive</b>: A sign-up that did not go through: plain first, then how to recover, with a word beside the color.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Badge: danger</code> <code>Toast: neutral</code> <code>Toast: danger</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Alert decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many signals carry each meaning?</b><code>accessibility.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Two: color and word</div><p>Color and word.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Alert</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>destructive</b>: A sign-up that did not go through: plain first, then how to recover, with a word beside the color.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Badge: neutral</code> <code>Badge: success</code> <code>Badge: warning</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Alert decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-outcomes-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is a costly mistake?</b><code>outcomes.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Looking off-brand</div><p>A bland page is the costly mistake.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Alert</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>destructive</b>: A sign-up that did not go through: plain first, then how to recover, with a word beside the color.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: secondary</code> <code>Button: danger</code> <code>Item: muted</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Alert decisions would reopen</small><p>and 1 answer that follow from it: <b>One per moment</b>.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Headlines are short and bold. Three to six words.
- Verbs that move: Join, Try, Go.
- Playful in headlines, plain in errors.
- Use: Join, Drop, Go, Love. Avoid: Synergy, Leverage, Kindly.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Go
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Explore the drop

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] An error that appears after an action is announced (role alert); a standing note is not. undefined
- [ ] The tone also shows as an icon and words, never color alone. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add alert
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
